events.text: Your first night in the county prison. The straw is wet, the rice is grey, and the man in the next cell will not stop singing.

effects.log: By dawn the whole block is singing. The guards give up and join in.
You find a stillness under the noise. Prison is a strange kind of seclusion.

events.text: The old man in the corner cell has been here forty years. The guards are afraid of him, and nobody says why.

effects.log: He eats it slowly, then taps your wrist twice. "Your breathing is wrong." He fixes it in a sentence.
Wise, perhaps. At night you hear him breathing like a tide.

events.text: In the prison yard, a gang boss decides your rice is his rice.

ok.log: He tests you once. After that the yard gives you room.

fail.log: His gang teaches you prison manners.

effects.log: He is surprised. You have made a strange sort of friend.

events.text: Your cellmate has been digging a tunnel behind the latrine bucket for three years. It is nearly done. He invites you.

ok.log: Out under the wall at midnight. The river carries you to freedom.

fail.log: The tunnel collapses. Guards drag you both out, and the warden watches you closely from then on.

effects.log: He goes alone. You never learn if he made it.

events.text: A guard lets it be known that ten taels would lose your paperwork somewhere very far away.

effects.log: Your name vanishes from the rolls. You walk out with the morning rubbish.
He shrugs. Your rice gets greyer.

events.text: A letter reaches you in prison, the seal already broken by the warden. It is from someone who has not forgotten you.

effects.log: It says nothing important. It means everything.
You scratch your answer into the stone. Someone will read it someday.

events.text: The warden's son is sick, and the prison physician is drunk. The warden has heard you know herbs.

ok.log: The fever breaks. The warden remembers it kindly.

fail.log: The boy recovers slowly, no thanks to you.

effects.log: The warden remembers. Your cell gets draughtier.

events.text: The prisoners are sent to rebuild the city wall. Stones, sun and a whip that is mostly for show.

effects.log: Your body grows hard as the stones.

choices.text: Work slowly and watch the guards

effects.log: You learn their shifts. It might be useful.

events.text: A new emperor's accession: an amnesty is announced for minor crimes. Your name is on the list, spelled wrong.

effects.log: Nobody checks the spelling. You are free.
The clerk is so surprised by your honesty that he lets you out anyway.

events.text: A riot breaks out over the rice. Torches, shouting, and a gate left open in the chaos.

ok.log: You are three streets away before anyone counts heads.

fail.log: A guard catches your collar at the gate and drags you back inside.

effects.log: You hold a doorway so the old men are not trampled. The warden notices.

events.text: A young thief in your block begs you to teach him to fight so he can survive when he gets out.

effects.log: Every night, in the dark, stance by stance. He is released a year before you, and waves from the gate.
Harder. Better. He writes you letters after he gets out.

events.text: Stone walls, one window, nothing to do but breathe. Some masters seek this silence on purpose.

effects.log: A season of perfect stillness. Your internal energy deepens.
Push-ups on the stone floor, a thousand a day.

events.text: The warden calls you in. 'Good behaviour,' he says, as if it pains him. The gate opens early.

effects.log: The sky is very big.
He looks surprised. "Do not come back," he says, almost kindly.

events.text: The old man in the corner cell tells you his name at last. It is in the history books, under 'died in battle, forty years ago'.

effects.log: He nods. Before you leave, he teaches you a technique no one has seen in forty years.
'Out there,' he says, 'people want things from that name.'

events.text: Someone is smuggling meat buns into the prison in a laundry basket. The price is a favour.

choices.text: Buy a bun with a favour

effects.log: You carry a message for the smuggler. You never learn what it said.
The buns stop. So do the smiles in your block.
